description: The interface with a single `Dispose()` method that releases a resource deterministically instead of waiting for the garbage collector.
`using var x = ...;` disposes `x` at the end of the enclosing scope, even when an exception or a `return` leaves it early.
The interface whose `DisposeAsync()` returns a `ValueTask`, for cleanup that needs I/O, consumed with `await using`.
The rule that whoever creates a disposable object disposes it, while services injected by the container are disposed by the container.
The protected virtual method a non-sealed class uses so derived classes can add cleanup, with `disposing` true from `Dispose()` and false from a finalizer.
A built-in wrapper for an unmanaged handle that already provides the finalizer, so your own classes almost never need one.
The exception thrown when code uses an object after it was disposed, typically an injected service someone disposed too early.
